SERVED

SERVED

SIX LOST THINGS

THE BELT
A slow belt carries flat, cleared things past the hooks: a hat, a clock, a small bell.
The belt runs on into a chute lit by a single red lamp. The lamp is a lens. It turns toward the Hollow, and the circle blinks once.
The camera pulls back. The Hollow is quiet.
The causeway is stone slabs over a pit of mist. A pair of lamps burns at each stop, one for every leg.
The circle stands. Slice and Wallit are on the books. Thanks for playing.

THE CLEARING FLOOR
Beyond the broken gate a yard lies sunken in the dark, lit by lamps along a slow conveyor.

THE GATE
No handle. No hinges. No doormat. Wallit knocks with the bat.

THE HALF-BUILT
The belt has stopped. In the chute, the Half-Built Yo Bot still hangs by one hook, one claw out, wanting finishing.
The last pair of lamps. Ahead the slabs end in the mist, and something tall is walking up them, slowly, to wait.

THE LAST STAMP
The order drops, unsigned. The ring on the grass waits for one more stamp.
The lever drops. Down the line the hooks swing empty, and the belt coughs and stops.

THE LONG WALK
A causeway of stone slabs runs out over a pit of mist, six lamps on either side. A single path. No cover.
The Moonlit Hollow, changed. The wall of the Department is a row of broken stumps, and a path of pale slabs runs out to nothing.

THE MOONLIT HOLLOW
The wall is gone. A path of pale slabs leads out of the Hollow and stops at nothing. The circle is brighter than it has ever been.

THE NOTICE
The Courier comes apart. Its notice drifts down onto the grass. Nobody has signed it.

THE ORDER, READ ALOUD
The Foreman steps off its plinth, the order held flat on its chest. It holds the sheet out to be read. In the cleared pile by Wallit's boot lies a hat-tag from the belt.
The paper reads: STRIKE THIS ADDRESS. No signature. The Server's leg unfolds.

THE PLACE DEPARTMENT
Where things that should not exist are given an address.

THE READING ROOM
A bare round hall. The circle is drawn on its floor at the size of the Hollow's. The walls are lined with forms, all identical, all this order. In the middle, a desk. Empty.

THE REGISTRAR
A gold Spider Bot with a ledger on its back takes the desk. It opens the first page and begins to read.

THE RISE
A plate catches the lantern light on the far rise. INVALID, it says, in red. It is coming down the hill.
The Server's last paper slides along the slab, addressed to the circle. Slice looks at it.
The Spider Bot comes apart. The order drops.
The stamp comes down. For the first time it says ADDRESS, and nothing strikes it. Every lost thing in the Hollow gets a door.

THE STAMP
Out of the dark comes a stamp: RETURN TO SENDER. Its ink is the only bright thing in the Hollow.
The stamp prints ADDRESS. Nothing strikes it. Every lost thing in the Hollow gets a door.

THE STAMP, REVERSED
He presses the Department's own stamp to the first page. The ink shows nothing, then DENIED. Every form on the walls turns over at once, blank.
The wall answers. From the other side, pressed through the dark, the same stamp: RETURN TO SENDER.
